title: Read a .def file
description:
Write a reader for the `EXPORTS` lines of a module-definition file.

```cpp
struct DefExport
{
    std::string name;        // the public name
    std::string internal;    // the function in the code; the same as name when there is no "= ..."
    int ordinal{ -1 };       // -1 when no @number is given
    bool noName{ false };    // NONAME
    bool data{ false };      // DATA
};

std::vector<DefExport> readDef(const std::string& text);
```

Rules:

- Lines are separated by `\n`. Leading and trailing spaces do not matter.
- Skip blank lines, comment lines starting with `;`, the `LIBRARY` line and the `EXPORTS` line itself.
- Every other line is one export: `name`, optionally `= internal`, optionally `@number`, then optionally the words `NONAME` and `DATA` in any order. Words are separated by spaces; `=` and `@` may have spaces around them or not.

```
LIBRARY StoneMath
EXPORTS
    stackHeight       @1
    internalCounter   @3   DATA
    debugDump         @4   NONAME
    StackHeight = stackHeight
```

gives four exports: `{stackHeight, stackHeight, 1}`, `{internalCounter, internalCounter, 3, data}`, `{debugDump, debugDump, 4, noName}`, `{StackHeight, stackHeight, -1}`.
hints: Before splitting a line into words, put spaces around `=` and before `@`. Then `Pub=impl@7` becomes `Pub = impl @7` and every case looks the same.
